# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — first capability from an empty seed: grader contract (literal values, data_only openpyxl in place) + inspect→solve→verify→finish procedure
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new; the empty seed sent no system message):
    - the grader contract (no recalculation; formula strings read as empty) → cluster A;
    - openpyxl data_only in-place writes to answer_position only, with the reasons to_excel breaks → B;
    - save only the data_only copy → C;
    - logic rules (Excel coordinates, labels, pre-filled examples as a test, float tolerance, append semantics, exact names, create a missing target sheet) → D;
    - a worked example;
    - a finishing checklist → E.
  - task_template.md (new; replaces the built-in): the same fields plus an "Unnamed: N"/row-index warning, and a 4-step procedure (Inspect → Solve → Verify → Finish with a no-code reply). The built-in line "once that file exists, you are done" is removed → D, E.
- Expected effects and why they're safe:
  - A should fix most of 37378, 46897, 56563, 8942, 6698, 7902, 55049, 53647, 9569, 54144, 55979, 53383 and 37456 (logic permitting).
  - B/C/D should fix 227-40, 48527, 50768, 80-42, 59196, 267-18 and 51-12. Each was confirmed locally with the real compare_workbooks.
  - Passers already write literals. The openpyxl method is a recommendation; 382-10 (delete → None) and 402-43 (missing target sheet) are explicitly covered.
- Building on prior results: none; this is the first iteration.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet. Locally, keeping the agent's pandas logic and only switching the write to openpyxl (formula mode) still FAILED. The data_only load plus correct logic was required.
- Clusters not yet cracked: pure interpretation errors where even the right method gives a wrong answer (the remaining failures in 43436, 39046 and others), and preview-induced row confusion (the preview is adapter-owned).
- Plateau signal: n/a.
- Focus next iteration:
  - read the RESULT broke/fixed;
  - if any Sheet-Level passer broke, narrow rule #2 to Cell-Level, or soften it;
  - check that the "reply with no code" finish is actually honoured;
  - then mine the remaining failures for interpretation sub-clusters.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.875 Δ=+0.425 · fixed={227-40, 267-18, 37378, 39046, 46897, 48527, 51-12, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569} · broke={2768} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy: started from an empty seed. I diagnosed against the real grader instead of the trajectory feedback text: I replayed corrected outputs through the vendored compare_workbooks. This separated "wrong logic" from "wrong write method" (formula strings, formula-mode load, to_excel offsets). The write-method clusters were about half of all failures and are fixable with a single contract section.
- Lesson: fix scripts that kept the agent's logic but changed only the write method still failed. Verify a cluster fix end to end (data_only load + correct logic + literal write) before claiming it.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- What to try next: read the RESULT. If val is up but some passer broke, the likely culprit is the openpyxl-over-to_excel recommendation on Sheet-Level tasks. Then sub-cluster the residual interpretation failures, e.g. summary-table layouts and matrix lookups.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## from cand_0001 (spreadsheetbench)
- A ready-made "replay a candidate output through the scorer" helper (init → agent code → compare_workbooks) would save each optimizer from rebuilding one under /tmp. It is the single most useful verification tool for this benchmark.
- The trajectory `feedback` only says pass/fail per range. Including the first mismatching cell (expected vs got, e.g. "G1: want 42, got None") would make the formula-string and cached-value clusters visible without a local replay.
- The fact that an empty prompt.md means NO system message (not the default prompt) is documented only in the adapter source. Stating it in INSTRUCTIONS.md would help the first iteration.

files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Candidate cand_0001. The seed was EMPTY: prompt.md was blank, so no system message was sent, and the built-in task template was used. Baseline val = 0.450, i.e. 18/40 tasks. The metric is hard_no_recalc: the grader opens the output with openpyxl `data_only=True` and never recalculates.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula strings written as answers | 37378, 37456, 46897, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 6698, 7902, 8942, 9569 (13) | Asked for "a formula", the agent writes `=...` text into cells. The grader reads the cached value without recalculating, so it gets None | KNOWLEDGE (grader contract unknown to agent) | add sourced rule + output contract + worked example |
| 2 | B. Whole-sheet pandas rewrite / row offset / clobbering | 227-40, 48527, 39046, 50768, 43436, 80-42, 59196 (7) | `df.to_excel` shifts rows by the header/index offset, writes NaN, and overwrites cells outside the target; wrong pandas-to-Excel row mapping | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL | contract (openpyxl in place, exact coordinates) + coordinate-mapping rule |
| 3 | D. Interpretation / logic (labels, pre-filled examples, float threshold, append semantics) | 51-12, 80-42, 39046, 59196 (overlap with B) | Agent never inspects the real cells, ignores pre-filled example answers, uses exact float `>=`, and decides "already done" instead of appending | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure in template (inspect → solve → verify → finish) + rules |
| 4 | C. Cached values lost by loading in formula mode | 267-18 | `load_workbook()` without data_only drops the cached values of the answer-range cells that hold original formulas | KNOWLEDGE | rule: always save the data_only copy |
| 5 | E. No verification / identical-code loops to 30 turns | many of the above | Template said "once that file exists, you are done"; there was no verify step and no finish signal | BEHAVIORAL | replace line with verify + "reply without code to finish" |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | add sourced rule + reason; tighten output contract | prompt.md "How your work is graded" + Output contract #1 | States the grader's actual behavior (data_only, no recalculation, 2-decimal rounding, exact text) and requires computed literal values even when a formula, VBA or macro is requested. This holds for every task under hard_no_recalc | Yes. All 18 passers already write literal values, as their passing proves |
| B | contract (recommended method) + reason | prompt.md Output contract #2–#4 | Recommends openpyxl `data_only=True` in place, writing only answer_position at Excel coordinates. Says why to_excel fails, keeps pandas for reading, and covers creating a missing target sheet | Framed as a recommendation, not a ban. Passers whose to_excel output was correct stay correct under openpyxl. 402-43 (target sheet absent from the input) is covered by the create_sheet line |
| C | add rule | prompt.md Output contract #2 + "existing formulas" bullet | Load data_only. Read formulas from a second copy only; never save that copy | Neutral for passers |
| D | ordered procedure + rules | task_template.md "How to work" step 1–2; prompt.md "Getting the logic right" | Inspect real cells (headers, labels, pre-filled examples, max_row); use the examples as a test; float tolerance; append semantics; copy names exactly; "Unnamed: N" preview hint | Inspection is read-only; it does not change any passer's answer |
| E | replace an over-strong line; add finish signal | task_template.md steps 3–4; prompt.md "Finishing" | Replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with: reopen and verify, then reply with NO code to finish. This matches the adapter loop: a no-code reply after a solution ends the episode, and a verify round does not change the solution code | The adapter replays the code from the last round that changed the output, so verify rounds cannot overwrite a solution |
| all | role/goal line; worked example | prompt.md role line + `<example>` | A single compact example that pins the shape: load data_only, literal write, save, read back | — |

## Verify-the-fix
- A (37378, 46897, 56563, 8942): I replayed corrected solutions locally with the real `compare_workbooks` (`/tmp/dx/v/t*.py`). Pattern: openpyxl data_only, compute in Python, literal write, save. Each went from FAIL to PASS. The original trajectories wrote `=...` strings, which graded as None.
- B (227-40, 48527, 39046, 50768, 80-42, 59196): the same harness with the openpyxl in-place write at exact coordinates gave PASS. The agents' to_excel outputs had shifted rows or clobbered cells and FAILED.
- C (267-18): data_only load + save keeps the cached G1 value → PASS. A formula-mode load + save → G1=None → FAIL. Reproduced both locally.
- D (51-12): the float-tolerance comparison gives PASS. A plain `>=` misses the exact 110% row → FAIL (reproduced). For 80-42, appending after the last used row → PASS.
- E: cannot be replayed offline because it is model behavior. I checked it against the adapter source (lines ~1419–1460): a no-code reply after solution_code is set → break. Verify rounds decrement verify_left without changing solution_code.
- Template contract: the adapter's own `_task_template_error(cand_dir)` returns None, and `.format(...)` renders correctly.
- Blast radius: UNBOUNDED, because the prompt changes for all 40 tasks. Passing tasks most exposed: Sheet-Level passers that used to_excel (142-12, 382-10, 395-36, 402-43, 416-15, 463-17), which may now switch to openpyxl. I checked 382-10: the golden sets removed cells to None, which matches the new "set each removed cell to None" rule. I checked 402-43: Sheet2 is absent from the input, which the create_sheet rule covers.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees: none. Serial work, because the system instructions forbid Agent/Workflow unless the user requests them.
- Local replay harness against the vendored grader (`third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py`) on init/golden pairs, to confirm each cluster's fix pattern before writing prose.
- Prior iterations: none. RUNMAP, LEDGER and rejected.jsonl are empty; this is the first iteration.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The grader-contract section (data_only, no recalculation, literal values even when a formula is requested). It targets the largest cluster (13 tasks).
- Recommending openpyxl in place over to_excel, together with its reason.
- Template steps 3–4: verify, then finish with a no-code reply. Never restore "once that file exists, you are done".
- Pre-filled examples used as a test; float tolerance.

## Deliberately skipped
- Preview format changes ("Unnamed: N" headers, the 5-row limit): these live in the adapter, which is not editable. I mitigated them with prose instead.
- Task-specific logic for individual tasks (e.g. specific lookups): any such fix would be hardcoding. I covered them only through the general inspect/oracle procedure.
- I did not run a full evaluation, per the rules.

---

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.
